content:
sasha: thinking out loud — we should add a per-tier regional-penalty and model-fallback policy so free/standard tenants don't get routed cross-region for high-cost models. avoids 200ms+ egress for trivial demos. any objections?
kevin: +1 in principle. curious about how we calculate the penalty. e.g. is it absolute latency threshold or relative to local median?
taylor: prefer relative. a 100ms penalty on apac vs na is different if local median is 40ms vs 10ms. recommend percent over median + fixed floor.
maria: also need to consider model-variant quality: we can't silently fall back to an aggressive quantized variant for enterprise clients.
kevin: agreed. propose policy fields in routing config:

```yaml
region_routing:
  tier_penalties:
    free: {latency_margin_pct: 200, fixed_ms: 80}
    standard: {latency_margin_pct: 150, fixed_ms: 50}
    enterprise: {latency_margin_pct: 110, fixed_ms: 20}
  model_fallback:
    allow_fallback: true
    whitelist_variants: ["x16-q8", "x8-q4"]
    max_quality_drop: 0.07 # measured on eval set
```

kevin: fallback should be opt-in per-customer; default allow for free/standard, default deny for enterprise unless enterprise contract says otherwise.
sasha: UX note — console should show which region was chosen and the reason (latency vs quota vs tier_penalty) and, if a fallback happened, what variant and expected quality delta.
taylor: telemetry: add tags to traces: region_chosen, penalty_reason, fallback_variant, fallback_quality_est. that'll make alerts for regression easy.
maria: ops: add a circuit-breaker if fallback variant error rate > 3% for 5min, revert to previous model or route to fallback region.
kevin: small nit — we should avoid oscillation: if we prefer local region but transient probe spikes happen, add hysteresis / min-stable-window per-session (e.g., 30s sticky)
sasha: yep. sticky session + exponential backoff for probes. also add a "graceful degrade" UI in console to preview how a tenant would be routed under current config.

maria: can we store per-tenant override in tenant config? customers may request hard-region pinning.
kevin: yes: tenant.config.routing_override = {region: eu-west-1, ignore_penalties: true} but only allowed for enterprise and with admin approval.
sasha: action items:
- kevin: draft RFC for config schema + validation (including max_quality_drop enforcement)
- taylor: telemetry fields + console UX mockup for routing decision trace
- maria: ops runbook for fallback circuit-breaker + rollback
- sasha: add API change to include chosen_region & fallback_variant in /v1/response-metadata

kevin: I'll put the RFC up tomorrow. cc @deploy-bot for a quick lint on schema.
deploy-bot: schema-lint passed on local branch. test-suite: 213 passing, 3 flaky.

taylor: OK, we should also add a small simulated playbook in the console: "simulate routing for tenant X from ip Y" — shows candidate regions, latencies, penalties, chosen model variant.
sasha: love it. reduces support back-and-forth.
maria: +1. also log a discrete event for any fallback so PMs can analyze feature regressions.
kevin: question — how do we measure "max_quality_drop" in prod? we only have eval snapshots.
sasha: tie it to canned evals per-variant + soft runtime monitors (embedding drift, token-level perplexity proxies). start with eval and then add runtime alerts.
taylor: ok. I'll prototype the console card and telemetry schema and share by EOD.

maria: anything else? otherwise I'll draft the ops runbook and include the ejection thresholds.
kevin: nope. sounds good. thanks.

sasha: thanks all :thumbsup:
